You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Solved test with one wrong guess and two demos. Useful rule evidence for recurring task family.

## Demonstrations
Demo 1: 25x17, background 6, marker pattern color 8. Grid has two independent row-segment cases, with horizontal runs of 8s and structured surrounding pixels. Output adds color 1 to the empty cells immediately following a horizontal contiguous 8-run, extending it to the right boundary:
- At row 7 (0-indexed), a run of 8s ends at col15; output sets col16 to 1 (one cell only in this demo's 17-wide grid; note rest of the row was background).
- Rows 8-9 run extends through cols11-15; output sets col16=1 in both rows.
The output specifically changes only the adjacent cell(s) after the run, not all remaining cells. This was initially misinterpreted.

Demo 2: 18x23, background 2, horizontal bars of color7. Partial bars from left edge end before right boundary. Output fills the remainder of each such row with color1:
- Row 6 bar through col16, cols17-22 become 1.
- Row 10 bar through col15, cols16-22 become 1.
Full-width bars unchanged. This distinguishes rule: for each horizontal bar/stripe of the foreground color, extend rightward from its endpoint to the right grid edge using color1; do not alter bars already touching the right edge.

Test 18x25: background3; partial color4 row6 occupies cols0-13, so correct output fills cols14-24 with 1. Full-width color4 row13 remains unchanged. All other rows remain 3. First guess (only put 1 at col14) was incorrect; second guess (fill all cells after the partial stripe to the right boundary) was correct.

## Operational lesson
A horizontal foreground segment that ends before the right edge is continued as color1 all the way to the right edge, leaving the original segment intact. Full-width stripes are unchanged. Color/background vary across instances; identify stripe color and dominant background, and preserve every other cell. Evidence may imply horizontal direction specifically toward the right edge."
